title: Slice Prioritization and Annotation Bidding Playbook
author: Aisha Raman
body:
Summary

This playbook describes a reproducible, cross-signal method for prioritizing prompt slices for annotation and evaluation when annotation budget is constrained. It introduces an annotation-bidding mechanism that allocates labeling budget to slices based on combined signals from production telemetry, eval harness deltas, quantization sensitivity, and historical regression triage. The goal is to surface high-impact slices for human review quickly while minimizing cost and time-to-action.

Goals

- Reduce mean time to detection and remediation for priority quality regressions by 30% for high-volume slices.
- Allocate annotation budget to slices with the highest expected utility (quality delta * traffic exposure / annotation cost).
- Integrate seamlessly with eval-harness, model-onboarding checks, quant profiles, and regression triage workflows.

Scope

- Applies to prompt slices derived from production telemetry, synthetic probe farms, and onboarding probe sets.
- Covers prioritization, auction/bid configuration, annotation assignment, and downstream integration with triage and rollout.
- Excludes detailed annotator instructions (see annotation-stewardship page) and labeling UI implementation details.

Definitions

- Slice: A traffic or probe partition defined by intent, API route, user cohort, template family, or other attributes.
- Signal: Any numeric input for prioritization (e.g., traffic volume, delta score, quant-sensitivity).
- Bid: A computed, unitless priority score used to order slices for annotation allocation.

Signals and Weighting

We combine multiple orthogonal signals into a single bid score. Signals below are normalized to [0,1] before aggregation.

- Traffic exposure (W_traffic): 7-day average request count for slice normalized by max slice volume.
- Delta severity (W_delta): Change in eval-harness failure rate or quality metric vs baseline (example: -ROUGE or increased hallucination rate).
- Regression recurrence (W_recurrence): Count of prior regressions or triage incidents involving the slice in the past 90 days, scaled to [0,1].
- Quant-sensitivity (W_quant): Sensitivity score from quantization profile tests (probing same prompt family at target quant levels).
- Cost-per-annotation inverse (W_cost): 1 - (estimated annotation cost / max expected cost) to favor cheaper high-impact slices.

Scoring formula (example)

Bid = alpha*T + beta*D + gamma*R + delta*Q + epsilon*C

Where T,D,R,Q,C are the normalized signals and alpha..epsilon are weights. Default weights: alpha=0.30, beta=0.30, gamma=0.15, delta=0.15, epsilon=0.10. We recommend tuning weights per product line.

Procedure: End-to-end prioritization and annotation allocation

1. Ingest slices into the prioritization service. Inputs: slice id, 7-day traffic, eval-harness delta metrics, quant-sensitivity vector, last 90d regression events, annotation-cost estimates.
2. Normalize signals and compute Bid per slice using the scoring formula.
3. Produce a ranked queue of slices and assign annotation budget in bidding rounds (see auction below).
4. Create annotation tasks in the annotation system with metadata: slice_id, priority (bid), schema, target labels, and TTL.
5. After annotation completes, results are fed into eval-harness and triage pipelines automatically: quality checks, delta re-computation, and regression alarm generation.
6. If annotations indicate a high-severity regression (see thresholds), trigger an immediate rollback or model fallback policy per regression triage runbook.

Auction / Bidding mechanism (budget-constrained rounds)

- Bidding rounds are 24-hour windows. Each round has a fixed annotation budget (tokens or USD) assigned by product/owner team.
- Slices bid based on computed Bid score; budget is allocated top-down until budget exhausted.
- Reserve up to 10% of budget each round for emergent slices flagged by SRE or urgent customer tickets.

Example allocation algorithm (pseudocode)

1. Sort slices by Bid desc.
2. For slice in sorted list:
   a. If slice.estimated_cost <= remaining_budget: assign full annotation block for slice.
   b. Else if remaining_budget > minimum_block: assign fractional sample proportional to remaining_budget and stop.

Annotation task definitions and sampling

- Block size: default 200 examples per full block (tunable by slice type).
- Minimum block: 25 examples (for exploratory sampling).
- Sampling strategy: stratified by route/intent and time-of-day to capture production variance.

Config table: prioritization service parameters

| Parameter | Description | Example default |
|---|---:|---:|
| weights | Comma-separated weights for T,D,R,Q,C | 0.30,0.30,0.15,0.15,0.10 |
| round_length_hours | Auction/bidding round length | 24 |
| default_block_size | Full annotation block size | 200 |
| min_block_size | Minimum exploratory block | 25 |
| reserve_budget_pct | Budget reserved for emergent slices | 10 |
| sensitivity_threshold | Quant-sensitivity threshold to mark "sensitive" | 0.6 |

CLI / API examples

- Compute bids for all active slices (example):
  $ rictl prioritize --space applied-ml --since 7d --weights 0.3,0.3,0.15,0.15,0.1 --out bids.csv

- Allocate annotation budget for a round:
  $ rictl allocate-annotation --round 2026-02-10 --budget-usd 2500 --reserve 10

- Export top N slices for annotation:
  $ rictl export-top --n 25 --format json --out /tmp/top25.json

Integration points and downstream actions

- Eval-harness: annotated labels are automatically ingested into the eval-harness dataset registry. New evaluations are scheduled using the same seed sets and metrics as the original reporting.
- Model-onboarding: onboarding runs include a prioritization pre-check so newly onboarded models immediately surface slices with high quant-sensitivity or coverage gaps.
- Regression triage: when annotated deltas exceed the triage severity threshold, the regression runbook is triggered and a triage ticket is created with links to annotated evidence and scalar plots.
- Observability: per-slice dashboards expose traffic, bid evolution, annotation status, and post-annotation delta.

Monitoring and SLOs

- Annotation turnaround SLO: 48 hours for full block annotations on high-priority slices (bid in top 10%).
- Detection SLO: 95% of slices that cross the triage severity threshold should be annotated within two bidding rounds.
- Budget adherence: allocate <= 5% variance vs planned monthly annotation USD budget.

Decision thresholds and escalation rules

- Triage severity threshold: post-annotation delta >= 5% absolute regression in the primary quality metric (or a configurable alternative).
- Hot-slice escalation: if a slice shows >3 separate increments in delta across three successive rounds, escalate to oncall-evals for manual investigation.

Ownership and responsibilities

- Prioritization service owner: applied-ml platform team (pager: #applied-ml-prio).
- Annotation ops: data platform / annotation stewardship.
- Eval-harness integration: eval-platform team.
- Regression triage automation: model-reliability team.

Rollout plan

1. Pilot (2 weeks): run with 5 product slices, manual annotation handoff. Verify scoring signal alignment and label quality.
2. Beta (6 weeks): expand to 25 slices across two product lines; enable automated annotation task creation.
3. GA: enable full auction rounds, integrate reg triage triggers, and publish dashboards.

Rollback criteria

- Stop automated allocations if annotation quality (inter-annotator agreement) falls below 0.7 for two consecutive rounds.
- Revert to manual prioritization if the prioritization score shows instability (top-10 composition churn > 40% between rounds) for three rounds.

Frequently asked questions

Q: How are annotation-cost estimates derived?
A: Cost estimates are historical-cost-based per-label type and slice complexity heuristics (token counts, multi-turn context). They are recalibrated monthly.

Q: Can product teams override bids?
A: Yes — product owners can flag slices as "owner-priority" which adds a fixed boost (default +0.2) to the bid for a configurable number of rounds. Overrides are audited.

Appendix A: sample prioritization JSON payload

{
  "slice_id": "checkout-abort-001",
  "traffic_7d": "4320",
  "eval_delta": "0.078",
  "quant_sensitivity": "0.42",
  "regression_count_90d": "1",
  "estimated_annotation_cost_usd": "120"
}

Appendix B: tuning notes

- For low-volume enterprise routes, increase beta (delta weight) to 0.45 to emphasize quality impact over traffic.
- For quant-migration windows, temporarily set delta=0.2, quant=0.4 to prioritize sensitivity discovery.
